name: When should I consider replacing my water heater instead of repairing it?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider replacing my water heater instead of repairing it?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should consider replacing your water heater when repairs become frequent and costly, or if the unit is old, typically over 10-12 years. Signs like a leaking tank, significant rust in the hot water, or a complete lack of hot water due to a major internal failure often indicate that replacement is more economical than repair. Newer models offer improved energy efficiency, which can lead to long-term savings on utility bills. We can help you assess whether repair or replacement is the best option for your home.
acceptedAnswer.description: Consider replacement if your water heater is over 10-12 years old, requires frequent repairs, or has major issues like a leaking tank.
